work: title: Zirāʻat-nāmah; زراعت نامه
author: name(s): Anonymous
paratext: incipit: Az hikmat-i rabbani waz faid-i khur u baran Has the same incipit as the work listed by Storey under Kitab-i Zira'at, but in the colophon of this MS the work is referred to as Zira'at-namah. A treatise on Indian agriculture.
bibliography: note(s): Folio one, recto: a) signature: C.J. Doyle etc b) Stamp, the name entered in ink: Presented to the ROYAL ASIATIC SOCIETY by Colonel Doyle. English marbled paper cover.
bibliography: bibl: Storey, II, iii, pp. 376, 378.; Entered in the Donations Register for 15 March 1834. No 17 in list of Persian MSS.

work: title: Takhmīs al-burdah; تخميس البردة
author: name(s): Būṣīrī, Sharaf al-Dīn Muḥammad ibn Saʻīd, 1213?-1296? البوصيري، شرف الدين محمد بن سعيد أبو عبد الله الصنهاجي
paratext: incipit: ما بال قلبك لا ينفك ذا ألم
paratext: explicit: مارتحت عذبات البان ريح صبا واطرب العيس حادي العيس بالنغم
bibliography: note(s): The text of Busiri's poem the Burdah with the amplification by Nāṣir al-Dīn Muḥammad al-Fayyūmī ناصر الدين محمد الفيومي

work: title: Kitāb uṣūl al-handasah wa-al-ḥisāb; كتاب اصول الهندسة والحساب
author: name(s): Euclid اقليدس
paratext: incipit: وبعد فلما فرغت من تحرير المجسطي رأيت ان احرر كتاب اصول الهندسة والحساب المنسوب إلى إقليدس الصوري
paratext: explicit: قد اتفق فراغ المصنف من تحرير هذا الكتاب وتصنيفه ثانى عشرين من الشعبان المعظم سنة ست واربعين وستمايه وقد فرغ من تحريره اضعف العباد وقد اوشكته تسعه 14 سنه 914 ربيع الثاني
bibliography: note(s): Arabic translation of Euclid's Geometry bound in green shagreen with pages in the wrong order.

work: title: Dīvān-i Khayālī; Divan-ı Hayâlı̂; ديوان خيالي
author: name(s): Hayâlı̂, -1557 Khayālī خيالي
paratext: incipit: دلا بو منزل ويرانى صنمه جاى سرور که قصر دهره بولینور هزار درلو قصور
paratext: explicit: محبت خارته در کو کلم ازلدن عشقی جانا قویر پر ماز شرع بر طاش قدیمی اوله هر خانه

work: title: Seyahatname; Siyāḥatnāmah; سياحتنامه; سياحت نامه
author: name(s): Evliya Çelebi, 1611?-1682? اوليا چلبى، محمد
paratext: incipit: الحمد لله الذي شرف المشرفين...و بعد دعا و خير ثنا اول ظلل الله روى زمين نظام الارضين اولان السلطان بن السلطان السلطان غازي مراد خان
bibliography: note(s): Vol.1 (Books 1 and 2) and vol.2 (Boooks 3 and 4) of Evliya's travels.

work: title: Jāmiʻ al-qawānīn; جامع القوانين
author: name(s): Kanawjī, Khalīfah Shāh Muḥammad, active 17th century Khalīfa Shāh Muḥammad قنوجی، خلیفه شاه محمد خلیفه شاه محمد
paratext: incipit: Sitayish u niyayish mar khuday-ra (sic, for ahadi-ra)
bibliography: note(s): Inside front cover: armorial bookplate of Gordon of Buthlaw. Inside back cover, printed slip, perhaps from a sale catalogue: Pand Nama of Saadi : Jamiu'l-Kawanin, being a Collection of Forms of Letter-writing &c. and another Work on Epistolary Correspondence. I vol. loose. Headings and punctuation in red. Numerous glosses in red in earlier part.
bibliography: bibl: Storey, iii, pp. 313-5.; Rieu, i, pp. 414-5.; Ethe No 2097.; General Gordon's bequest of books and Turkish, Perian and Arabic manuscripts is mentioned, without details in the donations register under November 6 1841. The bequest is mentioned in J.R.A.S., vii, 1843, Annual Report, p. x, and the manuscripts are briefly listed in the Proceedings, pp. xxx-xxxi. According to Morley's handwritten catalogue the manuscript came from Major David Price, but this is evidently a mistake; the manuscript is listed in J.R.A.S. vii.

work: title: Inshāʼ-i Harikarn; انشاء هركرن
author: name(s): Harikaṇa, Multānī Harkarn son of Mathurdas Multani
paratext: incipit: Hamd u sanay [sic for thanay, seemingly] mar hadrat-i Izad-i muta'al
bibliography: note(s): On watermarked European paper. aIn contrast to Codrington/Reade No 225 the title Irshad al-Talibin is not mentioned in the preface of this MS (nor in many others).

work: title: Anvār-i Suhaylī
author: name(s): Kāshifī, Ḥusayn Vāʻiẓ, d. 1504 or 5
paratext: incipit: Incipit (f2a): ... padishahan-i buzurg-ra dar qawa'id-i jahandari
bibliography: note(s): There appears to be no record of the registration of the MS before it was entered in Codrington/Reade. It is not among the handwritten additions on the Library copy of Codrington. Defective at beginning and end. The first folio is an irrelevant replacement from the beginning of the Gulzar-i Ibrahim of Zuhuri, mentioning Ibrahim 'Adil Shah. The Anwar-i Suhaili here starts in the account of the discovery of the book in India. Some use of red for headings and punctuation.

work: title: al-Wāfiyah fī sharḥ al-kāfiyah; الوافية فى شرح الكافية
author: name(s): Ibn Sharaf Shāh, Ḥasan ibn Muḥammad, 1247 or 8-1315 or 16 استراباذي، حسن بن محمد ابن شرف شاه، حسن بن محمد
paratext: incipit: بسم الله الرحمن الرحيم...وبعد فاني بعد ان شرحت كتاب الكافية في النحو اولا مع ايرادات واجوبة وابحاث كثيرة شرحته ثانيا
paratext: explicit: تمت الوافية فى شرح الكافية ...في يوم الست من شهر الرجب في سنة خمس وتسعين فثمانية وكتبه طاهر ابن طاهر
bibliography: bibl: Commentary on al-Kāfiyah fī al-naḥw of الكافية فى النحو Ibn al-Ḥājib, ʻUthmān ibn ʻUmar, 1175-1249 ابن الحاجب، عثمان بن عمر

work: title: Khuṭūṭ-i Sivājī; خطوط سواجی
author: name(s): Shivaji, Raja, 1627-1680 شواجی، راجا
paratext: incipit: Niwishtah Nil Prabhu? Munshi az Maharah Siwaji
bibliography: note(s): So in the MS; often Shivaji / [by various authors]; Inside front cover, printed slip: Lieut. Col. Briggs. Third fllyleaf, verso: (Briggs). Most of the MS is left blank. Letters, Firmans. and documents relating to the transactions between the Mahrattas and Aurangzib, Headings and punctuation in red.
bibliography: bibl: Not in Storey, Rieu or Ethe.

work: title: Manāfiʻ-i aḥjār (The beneficial properties of stones).
author: name(s): ʻAṭṭār ibn Muḥammad al-Ḥāsib
paratext: incipit: Naql kardah ast 'Attar b. Muhammad al-Hasib
bibliography: note(s): As Ellis 11 (1). Ff94b and 95 have a number of magical alphets. including one named after the astronomer Farghani, in red ink with the corresponding Arabic letters in black. By the scribe of the rest of the MS. For other details see Ellis 11 (1). On the properties of stones with information of those associated with the heavenly bodies and auspicious designs for seals for each one. Contains a number of lively illustrations of scenes to appear on magically effective seals.

work: title: Said-namah-i Khani.
author: name(s): Muhammad Salim Razi.
paratext: incipit: Sair-i ahang-i nawa'i kih 'andalib-i hazar-dastan
bibliography: note(s): Front flyleaf, recto: a) Signature of Ellis dated 16.6.04. b) prescription to improve the memory from the Imams 'Ali and Sadiq et al. Final folio, verso: a) In Ellis's hand: Hannan Watson & Co. b) Note recording completion of collation. A treatise on hunting in a preface and two chapters, with subdivisions, largely composed of descriptions of all kinds of fauna and the legal prescriptions for hunting. Headings and punctuation in red. Scribe: Possibly autograph. Dedicated to Shaikh 'Ali Khan (Zanganah).

work: title: A translation of the Dhakhirat al-Iskandar.
paratext: incipit: Wa in ast awwal-i kitab-i mutarjam
bibliography: note(s): Bound and uniform with Ellis 11 (2) and 11 (3). By the same scribe. F1a. Signature of A.G. Ellis. A work in ten sections (fann) on various aspects of magic, supposedly translated (into Arabic) from a Greek original. This version lacks the usual story of the discovery of the bookduring al-Mu'tasim's siege of Amorium in A.D. 838.. Headings in red. Contains several illustrations of inscriptions for talismans and a few blank spaces intended for others.
bibliography: bibl: Storey, ii, pp. 457-8.; Ethe, No 2804 (1) [?].; Manfred Ullmann, Die Natur- und Geheimwissenschaften im Islam, pp. 376-7.

work: title: Habib al-siyar. Vol. 1.
author: name(s): Khvānd Mīr, Ghiyās̲ al-Dīn ibn Humām al-Dīn, ca. 1475-1535? خواند مير، غياث الدين بن همام الدين
paratext: incipit: Rabbana atina min ladunika rahmatan wa hayyi' lina min amrina rushdan. latayif-i akhbar
bibliography: note(s): Front flyleaf, recto: Presented to the Oriental Translation Commi[ttee] by Sir A. Malet Bart. Folio one, recto: a) Large circular seal Amanat-dar Khan fidawi-yi Badshah-i Ghazi Muhammad Farrukhsiyar, dated 1124, regnal year 1. b) Note in Arabic recording transfer to Ahmad b. 'Ali. Incomplete. c) Effaced impression of large circular seal. Part of impression of small rectangular seal, trimmed down in repair. Inside back cover: armorial bookplate of Sir Cha Warre Malet. From the Creation to the History of the first four Caliphs. Illuminated initial opening, with decorative panel at top of f1a. ruled margins. Rubricated headings and punctuation.
bibliography: bibl: Storey, i, pp. 101-2, 104-9.; Rieu, i, pp. 96-7.; Ethe, No 76.

work: title: al-Kāmil fī al-taʼrīkh; الكامل في التاريخ
author: name(s): Ibn al-Athīr, ʻIzz al-Dīn, 1160-1233 ابن الاثير، عز الدين
bibliography: note(s): Leaves out of order. Incomplete, lacking beginning and end;

work: title: Farhang [A large Arabic-Persian dictionary]. Vol. I, From letter Alif to letter Sin.
author: name(s): Anon.
paratext: incipit: Incipit (MS starts with section on alif) : hamzah-i maftuh barayi chand chiz mi-ayad
bibliography: note(s): 13.75 by 9.5 ins. Folio one, recto: Presented to the Oriental Translation Com by by Sir A Malet Bt Final folio, verso: note on some of the surahs of the Qur'an. Headings and punctuation in red. The title Farhang (dictionary) appears on flyleaves and elsewhere. A substantial and serious work but since there is no introduction and end of the work is missing it is not easy to identify. There are many marginal additions. Could this be a draft?

work: title: Majma‘ al-inshāʼ; مجمع الانشا
author: name(s): Muḥammad Amīn Banī Isrāʼīl محمد امين بني اشرائيل
paratext: incipit: Mansha'-i nashw nama-yi nihal-i insha
bibliography: note(s): Incomplete, the text breaking off in the twenty-ninth section. Folio 1a. Note in Persian with the date 5 Safar 1190 (more likely than 1195), the remainder defaced and partly rewritten in another hand. This has evidently been taken as the date of copying, but there is no real reason to believe that. Flyleaves have several prayers, verses etc. on them, mostly difficult to read. Headings and punctuation in red. A collection of letters and other compositions in 30 sections (fasl)..
bibliography: bibl: Storey, iii, pp. 341-42.; Rieu, iii, pp. 1067-8.; Ethe, Nos 2122, 2943.

work: title: Amadnamah.
author: name(s): Anon
paratext: incipit: Amadan amadah biyayad
bibliography: note(s): Punctuation and glosses in Hindustani appear in most of the manuscript in red but not in the last folios. Paradigms of Persian verbs. The title Amadnamah appears in pencil on the first folio in Arabic script but is clearly in the hand of a European. Possibly it was written by Price and accepted by Morley. The text begins abruptly with the forms of the verb amadan = to come.

work: title: Dīvān-i ʻAzīzī; Divan-ı Azı̂zı̂; ديوان عزيزى
author: name(s): Azizi, Yedikuleli Mustafa, -1585 عزيزى
paratext: incipit: عرض ايدوب كل يوز نى بلبل كلراره سحر شه كل لطفنه بلبل ينه دوشدى مظهر
paratext: explicit: عمرى اولدقجه اكر پیر و جوان صقلیه اول کوهرى كور مز ريان

work: title: Tezkere-i Latifı̂ Çelebi; Taz̲kirah-i Laṭifī Chilibi; تذكرۀ لطفی چلبی
author: name(s): Latifı̂, 1491-1582 لطفي، عبد اللطيف Kastamonulu Latifı̂, 1491-1582
paratext: incipit: بسم الله الرحمن الرحيم مطلع موزون كلام قديم محامد مظومۀ فصاحتنظام و مدایح منشورۀ بلاغت انتظام
bibliography: note(s): Lives of Turkish poets with copious qotations of their poetry.

work: title: Sharḥ al-Mishkāt; شرح المشكوة
author: name(s): Ṭībī, al-Ḥusayn ibn Muḥammad, d. 1343 طيبي،الحسين بن محمد
paratext: incipit: الدفتر الثاني من شرح المشكوة للطيبي...باب الحصار وقوت الحج
paratext: explicit: وقع الفراغ في يوم الاربعاء شهر ربيع الثاني سنة خمس وستين وسبعماية
bibliography: note(s): The second volume of al-Tibi's commentary on the Mishkāt al-Maṣābīḥ of Khaṭīb al-Tibrīzī, Muḥammad ibn ʻAbd Allāh, fl. 1337

work: title: Yusuf u Zulaikha.
author: name(s): Anon.
paratext: incipit: Incipit, of added opening page: Bi-nam-i khudawand har du saray
bibliography: note(s): The number 243a comes from a handwritten note in the Library copy of Codrington. Four folios at the beginning and six at the end are written in a different hand. The colophon of the last of these states that they were written in London by Ghulam Haidar, of Chandannagar Frasdhanagar (?) in Bengal. Second front flyleaf, recto: Presented by Colonel J S Harriot to the Royal Asiatic Society. Authorship frequently, but incorrectly attributed to Firdausi.
bibliography: bibl: Storey (de Blois), v, 476-482.; Rieu, ii, pp. 545-6; Suppt., p. 133.

work: title: Shams al-ʻulūm wa-dawāʼ kalām al-ʻArab min al-kulūm; شمس العلوم ودواء كلام العرب من الكلوم
author: name(s): Nashwān ibn Saʻīd al-Ḥimyarī, d. 1178? نشوان بن سعيد الحميري
paratext: incipit: القطعة الثالثة عن كتاب شمس العلوم بسم الله الرحمن الرحيم بالصاد وما تعدها من الحرف في المصاعف والاساء فعل بفت الصا
paratext: explicit: تم السفر الرابع من كتاب شمس العلوم ودواء كلام العرب من الكلوم...في شهر جمادى الاخرة الذي بعده رجب وشعبان من شهور سنة ثلاث وتسعين والف من هجرة محمد المصطفى
bibliography: note(s): The third part of Shams al-ʻulūm beginning with the letter sad.

work: title: 'Alamgir-namah.
author: name(s): Munshi Muhammad Kazim b. Muhammad Amin.
paratext: incipit: Ay dadah b-'aql ziwar-i agahi (partau-i agahi in other copies.)
bibliography: note(s): Bound in after the front flyleaf is an index of the regnal years covered in the work written in the hand of Ellis, giving references to folios of the MS and the pages of the printed edition. The following blank folio, recto, has a note, perhaps in the hand of Ellis, describing the MS, which it sayswas bought in India by W. Beveridge in 1899-1900. It incorrectly states that it has the seal of Muhammad Shah, and, as a correction, that it was written in the reign of Akbar Shah II, which is mistakenly placed in the 18th century. F1a (as numbered): a) Note: 'Ata-yi sultani-yi TLSjani? b) impression of large round seal of 'Ali Muzaffar Khan, devotee of Muhammad Shah, dated regnal year 3 and A.H. 1133. c) Persian note of inspection, ninth regnal year. d) Signature of Ellis, with date 3.1.21. F332a. a) Note, not Wholly deciphered, written in Shahjahanabad in regnal year 6? of Muhammad Akbar Shah, referring to the writer's son. b) In the hand of Ellis: Luzac (Beveridge) 3.1.21. A history of the first ten years of the reign of Aurangzib, lacking the end of the account of the tenth year. Red headings and punctuation.
bibliography: bibl: Storey, i, pp. 585-7.; Rieu, i, p. 266.; Ethe, No 347.

work: title: Kitāb-i intiẓām-i ḥayāt; کتاب انتظام حیات
author: name(s): Dodsley, Robert, 1704-1764
language: text lang(s): Persian (and Hindustani and Arabic. The Persian comes between the others)
paratext: incipit: Ay salikan-i khittah-i khak
bibliography: note(s): A paraphrastic translation of Robert Dodsley's Economy of human life. Bound in at the front of the manuscript are four folios written by Major Pogson, telling us something of his circumstances and the origin of his translations. When he was Assistant Adjutant General the work was completed with the help of his preceptor, Maulavi Sayyid Karim Husain. It is submitted to the R.A.S. in the hope that it may replace the 'puerile tales and fables' usually provided for students of 'seminaries of Oriental learning.' On European paper watermarked: J. Rump 1825. A paraphrase translation of Robert Dodesley's Oeconomy of Human Life, in Hindustani, Persian and Arabic. Headings and punctuation in red.

work: title: Akhlāq-i Nāṣirī; اخلاق ناصری
author: name(s): Ṭūsī, Naṣīr al-Dīn Muḥammad ibn Muḥammad, 1201-1274
paratext: incipit: Hamd-i bi-hadd wa thana-yi bi-'add
bibliography: note(s): The last four folios are on different paper and in a different and later hand. The text breaks off abruptly. This is seemingly the later version of the text. Ruled margin and decorative arch on first page of text. Headings in red. In the earlier part the area with the text is tinted light brown.
bibliography: bibl: As for Codrington/Reade No 188.; Price's bequest is noted in the Journal for 1836, pp. xii-xiv (an obituary notice p. lx).

work: title: Ẓafar′nāmah; ظفر نامه
author: name(s): Sharaf al-Dīn ʻAlī Yazdī, d. 1454 شرف الدین علی الیزدی
paratext: incipit: Hamdan aktharan (sic; elsewhere kathiran) mubarakan li-man yu'ti al-mulka man yasha'u
bibliography: note(s): Front flyleaf, recto: title and deprecatory ownership note of Pir 'Uthman son of Muhammad Sa'id Katkhuda of Wali Effendi-zadah. Second front flyleaf: a) Note of acquisition by 'Abd al-Wahhab b. 'Abd al-Rahman. b) Note of price: 1,000 aqchahs. c) Note of acquisition by 'Abd al-Rahim Qadi of Bursa. d) Note of acquisition by Muhammad called Wahy-zadah, dated A.H. 1011. The remainder of the page is covered with notes in various hands, glosses, verses, bits of prose concerning Timur etc, many of them attributed, e.g. to Suyuti, Mu'izzi, Nizami et al. Mostly Arabic and Persian, a few phrases in Turkish. Verso: covered with verses, mostly attributed, including Turkish ones of Hamdi. Folio one, recto: a) at top, note of ownership, written in difficult ruq'ah. b) at bottom, note of acquisition by 'Ali b. Uwais. The remainder of the page is covered with inscriptions in various hands mostly verse quotations in Persian and Arabic, often attributed. After the end of the text are five pages, mostly bearing inscriptions in various hands, including glosses, verses quotations concerning Timur and his descendants. Attributions are given for many of these, e.g., [Ibn] 'Arabshah, Jami et al. On last page, recto, [owner's?] date of birth, early winter, 1 Jumadi I? 888, Rumi month AHTRUS (?). Inside back cover, armorial bookplate of Gordon of Buthlaw. A history of Timur. Iluminated panel above beginning of text. Ruled margins. Headings and punctuation in red. Ruled bands dividing verses in first few pages.
bibliography: bibl: Storey, i, pp. 283-8.; Rieu, i, p 173-5.; Ethe, No 173.; General Gordon's bequest of books and Turkish, Perian and Arabic manuscripts is mentioned, without details in the donations register under November 6 1841. The bequest is mentioned in J.R.A.S., vii, 1843, Annual Report, p. x, and the manuscripts are briefly listed in the Proceedings, pp. xxx-xxxi.

work: title: Dīvān-i Sayf-i Isfarangī; ديوان سيف اسفرنگی
author: name(s): Isfarangī, Sayf al-Dīn, 1185 or 1186-1267 or 1268 سيف الدين اعرج اسفرنگی Sayf al-Dīn Aʻraj Isfarangī
paratext: incipit: Ay zadah dar sukhanit 'iqd-i thurayya
bibliography: note(s): Two facing pages in the middle have a number of seal impressions, largely effaced. Last folio, recto: a number of seal impressions around colophon, largely effaced. Last folio, verso: verses, notes of possession, one of Muhammad Ja'far, and seal impressions, including two of ... Shah Mir, dated 1109. Front flyleaf, recto: printed form for number filled in with 272 in European numerals and with 'Diwan-i Saif Isfarangi' in Persian. The name occurs in the colophon, but is evidently an alteration. Attribution needs to be checked. Many poems in praise of officials of Khurasan, e.g. Fakhr al-Mulk, probably later twelfth or early thirteenth century. Incomplete decoration. All headings left blank.
bibliography: bibl: Rieu, ii, pp. 624-6.; Ethe, No 1059.; These are not closely similar to the R.A.S. manuscript.

work: title: Habib al-siyar. First two and part of the third chapter of Vol. III.
author: name(s): Khvānd Mīr, Ghiyās̲ al-Dīn ibn Humām al-Dīn, ca. 1475-1535? خواند مير، غياث الدين بن همام الدين
paratext: incipit: Ya rabb bi-thana-yi khwud sukhansazam kun
bibliography: note(s): Ends rther abruptly, but neatly at the bottom of the page. Second flyleaf, recto: Presented by Sir John Malcolm May 19. 1827. Part of the same work as Codrington/Reade No 46. History of the Mongols, Khans, Mamluks, Muzaffarids, and other contemporaries, and of Timur and his descendants. fHeadings in red. Ruled margins. Illumitated panel above beginning of text.
bibliography: bibl: As for Codrington/Reade No 46.; Malcolm's gift is described in the Donations Register for 19 May 1827 and in the Transactions for 1830, pp. xcix-c.

work: title: Favāʼid-i ṣafavīyah; فوائد صفويه
author: name(s): Qazvīnī, Abū al-Ḥasan ibn Ibrāhīm, fl. 1796 قزوینی، ابو الحسن بن ابراهیم
paratext: incipit: Jahan-padishaha khuda'i turast
bibliography: note(s): Donations Register for May 19 1827. First front flyleaf, recto: Presented by Sir John Malcolm May 19, 1827. A history of the Safavid family from its origin to AH 1216, anf of the rival dynasties that displaced them in the eighteenth century.. Headings and punctuation in red. Written in India for the refugee Safavid prince Sultan Muhammad Mirza.
bibliography: bibl: Storey, i, pp. 319-20.; Rieu, i, pp. 133-4.; Ethe, No 567.

work: title: Maʼās̲ir-i sulṭānīyah; مآثر سلطانیه
author: name(s): Maftūn Dunbulī, ʻAbd al-Razzāq 1762 or 1763-1827 or 1828 مفتون دنبلی، عبد الرزاق‏
paratext: incipit: ... barayi chapawul wa tatawul-i anha warid gardidah and
bibliography: note(s): Folio one, recto: Presented by Col. Monteith Dec 4. 1830 A pencilled marginal note in Codrington/Reade No 151 (2)notes that nearly twenty-five pages (of the printed edition) are lacking. The page Nos of the Tabriz edition have been marked in pencil in the margin and the note stands below the page No 258. This MS is the portion of the second part missing in Codrington/Reade No 151 (2). Headings in red. Cream-coloured European watermarked paper.

work: title: An enumeration of the times which each letter of the Alphabet occurs in the the first 30 Surahs of the Koran.
bibliography: note(s): Not in Morley Printed Catalogue. F1b. Impression of seal of Tipu Sultan, dated 1226 (last figureuncertain), probably in Tipu's Mawludi era, for which see Storey, i, 17. Contains poems from Khayyam, Nizami, Kalim, Salim, Sa'ib, Iltifat Khan, Hakim Rukna, Talib and others. On paper sprinkled with silver on one side, and in part with stencilled designs in gold in addition.

bibliography: note(s): 'This MS. is imperfect both at the beginning and the end. A commencement of one leaf, and a conclusion of two leaves, have been added in Shikastah, in order to make the volume complete, but these additions are not from the work of Sharaf ad-Din. The first eight leaves of the original portion of the MS. have been misplaced by the binder: they should be inserted at the end of the volume, one leaf being missing between them and tha last page as it now stands. Nearly one-fifth of the whole work is wanting at the beginning, and about seven leaves at the end.' Morley, Printed Catalogue. At point there are pencilled notes in the MS to similar effect, presumably written by Morley. After the inserted inclusion are six further inserted folios containing several elaborate letters. The names Muhammad Baqir Khan and Rukn al-Daulah mentioned. Folio preceding text, recto: Presented to the Oriental Translation Committee by Sir A. Malet Baronet Verso: pasted-in copy of the entry in Morley's Printed Catalogue. Final inserted folio at end: several library notes in shikasta ('ard dida shud; mulhahazah shud; dakhil-i kitabkhanah-i wala-yi ma shud) and also 'Aurangzib Padishah'. Inside back cover: armorial bookplate of Sir Chas. Warre Malet. Headings and some punctuation in red. Ruled margins. Scribe of inserted conclusion: Sayyid Nasrullah.

work: title: Sharh-i Diwan-i Hafiz.
paratext: incipit: Rabbana anzil 'alaina ma'idatan min al-sama'
bibliography: note(s): Bound before this work is a fragment (8 folios) of a similar work, but in a different format (18 lines to the page). The first page of this is probably itself a replacement perhaps by the scribe of the longer text. In its introduction the current date is given as A.H. 1077. A work of commentary on problems in Hafiz, the Risalah-i Ajwibah of 'Abd al-Wahid Bilgrami is mentioned unfavourably so he cannot be the author. F1a and preceding folio bear a number of poems etc. F1b: Several partly effaced seal impressions, mostly or wholly of ... Qasim Husaini. Secondary title-page: Signature of Ellis dated 18.3.09. Final folio of 33 (b), in Ellis's hand: Luzac (Sotheby - Alexander) A commentary on the poetry of Hafiz explaining it in the mystical sense. A secondary title-page written in A.H. 1256 by Mirza Husain 'Ali Harawi for Anderson Sahib Bahadur is now loose. On the verso it has a description of both, in fact all three, parts of the MS Author: aThe secondary title-page says Maulana Hilali, and the word Hilali, possibly a name, appears in a verse at the end of the text. The work has no introduction. Scribe is described as Yar Muhammad the traveller, from Kurduh Atak? in Benares. Red ruled margins. Some punctuation in red.

work: title: Dabistān-i madhāhib; An account of the religious creeds and philosophical systems of the East.
author: name(s): Mubad Shah? ; Fānī, Muḥsin, d. 1671 or 2 فاني، محسن
paratext: incipit: Ay nam-i tu sar-daftar-i atfal-i dabistan
bibliography: note(s): Not in Morley Printed Cat. The attribution of the work to Muhsin Fani has long been discredited. Morley believed that the author was Amir Dhu 'l-Fiqar 'Ali al-Husaini, known as Mobed Shah. However, the author was certainly a Parsi. Folios 712-734 contain an account of the fall of 'Abd al-Samad Khan in the fifth year of Farrukhsiyar, with some account of the Sikhs and the long story of Mir Muhammad Husayn of Mashad's career in India as the discoverer of a new path in the earlier eighteenth century. Some of the followers of this movement later go to Bengal but at present, A.H.1194, only some of women are said to still be alive. (?) The anonymous author hopes to write more on the subject. Not all very clear. This is written by the same scribe as the main work. In the list of donors at the beginning of his handwritten catalogue this MS is included under the donations of Sir John Markham, and not those of Sir John Malcolm. A note added under the description of the MS in the catalogue reads: Presd. by Sir John Malcolm May 19. 1827, and this also appears on f2a. Inside front cover, f1a, f2a: title in English and Persian, numbers etc. Rubricated headings and punctuation,
bibliography: bibl: Encyclopaedia of Islam, 2nd edition, s.v. Dabistan al-Madhahib.; Rieu, i, pp. 141-2.; Ethe, i, No 2542.

From the beginning it appears that this is a section of an encyclopaedia by Qadi 'Abd al-Nabi covering the Nizam Shahs of Ahmadnagar. The encyclopaedia was known as Dastur al-'Ulama and Jami' al-'Ulum. 'Abd al-Nabi was active in the earlier part of the eighteenth century. See Storey.

Pages 149-195 have numerous English interlinear and marginal glosses and notes in red ink, probably written by Sir Charles Malet. F1a: Presented to the Oriental Translation Com by Sir A. Malet Bart. Last additional folio, verso: note of death of an unidentified person on Wednesday, eve of Thursday 10 Jumada I A.H. 1193 (26 May 1779). Includes the Haft Pand of Mulla Hasan Kashi, a qasidah of Fuduli, the Shams al-Manaqib of Mirza Mu'izz? Fitrat, the Saqi-namah of Zuhuri, letters of Shah Tahmasp II to Muhammad Shah, of 'Abd al-mu'min Khan to Shah 'Abbas and the reply etc. Ruled margins and dividing panels. Headings and punctuation in red in parts. Illuminated panel over beginning of text. Two sections have lluminated initial openings (135-6, 149-50 by existing pagination.) Page 415 has a drawing of a peacock in ink, with, in the margin, an appropriate poem subscribed by Mir 'Ali Naqi al-Husaini, who may also have drawn the picture.

work: title: Tarjamah i Tarikh i Tabari.
author: name(s): Ṭabarī, 838?-923 الطبري
paratext: incipit: Qala Muhammad ibn Jarir fi khutbati 'l-kitab
bibliography: note(s): The last two folios are later, and in nasta'liq, probably of the fifteenth century. At the bottom of the last page, below the colophon, is a note saying that it was copied from the original MS. It can be accepted that this is correct. The first four folios are on different paper and there is no rubrication. The ruled margins are black. The hand is not the same as on the following folios but looks remarkably convincing as fourteenth-century naskh. This MS was selected by Muhammad Raushan as the base MS for his edition. Check and get details. Bound with Codrington/Reade No 22 (2). Abridged and adapted Persian translation of the History of Tabari. Has a very brief contuation taking the history of the Caliphs up to A.H. 529. Author of the Arabic history: Muhammad b. Jarir al-Tabari. Ruled red margins; headings and punctuation in red.
bibliography: bibl: Storey, i, pp. 61-5.; Rieu, i, pp. 68-70. Ethe, No 2.; For Malcolm's gift see the Donations Register for 19 May 1827 and the Transactions for 1830, pp. xcix-c.

bibliography: note(s): Donations Register for May 19 1827. An Epitome of the History of Persia from Kayumars to A.H. 1046 (A.D. 1636) in the reign of Safi I. Shah Safi and even the Safavid dynasty as a whole are spoken of as in the past. The work would appear to be incomplete, even though it ends quite neatly. Headings and punctuation in red. On European paper, partly cream-coloured with three red lines ruled across each page, partly blue.
bibliography: bibl: Storey, i, p. 242.; The MS may be unique, but except perhaps for the section on the Safavids the work is of very little interest.

An elaborate prose preface does not seem to name the compiler. Ruled margins and dividing panels. Some marginal headings etc in red. Illuminated initial opening. Headings of new items in text in black on illuminated panels. Leaves in gold in the corners of many panels of text. Paper of text sprinkled with gold and often intended to contrast with margins; margins at times tinted to contrast with white text. Preceding the text is a double page miniature of a meadow with trees among mountains, in margins decorated with floral scrolls.
bibliography: bibl: No reference to the possible compiler found. This may be the only copy.; See Donations Register for May 19 1827. (No 11?)

work: title: Tabaqat i Nasiri.

paratext: incipit: Al-hamdu [alif]lillahi alladhi [alif]la ibtida' li-wujudihi [sic]
bibliography: note(s): Apparently overlooked in Morley's Handwriten Catalogue. It is not No 75 which is a copy of Firishtah presented by Briggs. The text is full of inaccuracies throughout. This ends with a colophon, not original here, stating it is written by Minhaj i Siraj on 5 Rabi' I 650, evidently a mistake for 658. On f1b, f2a, and at end of text: impressions of oval seal of Ahmad, date 1097. A general History from the earliest times to A.H. 658. Ruled margins. Rubricated headings, punctuation and diagrams.
bibliography: bibl: Storey, i, pp. 68-70.; Rieu, i, pp. 68-70.; Ethe, No 14.; Some information about this MS in Raverty's translation.

work: title: Tarikh-i Jahangir-namah-i Salimi.

paratext: incipit: Ay nam-i tu sardaftar-i asrar-i wujud
bibliography: note(s): Foliation begins at one on present f26. Some folios near beginning and some elsewhere replaced, these are not foliated and mostly have red ruled margins. F7a (as numbered) has a marginal note dated 1173 concerning Muhammad Shah's appointment of Sarbuland Khan as Subadar of Ahmadabad, and the gifts given him etc. F170. Marginal notes. a) In large Persian hand, damaged, but by Jalal al-Bu[khari] stating that near Lahore he had read the book through in spite of the poor style of the text and his own incurable illness. b) By a son (?) of Jalal Bukhari, dated middle of Safar 1064.at Pinpalar (?) between two other obscure places. Folio one, recto: a) Stamp, the name filled in by hand: Presented to the ROYAL ASIATIC SOCIETY by John Romer Esq. b) Persian note giving the title of the work as Tarikh-i Jahangir-namah-i Salimi, which was written by Jahangir himself. with English translation. The so-called Garbled Memoirs of Jahangir, followed by the Pand Namah (ff127-150, as numbered) and concluding with a number of letters, petitions, etc, including correspondence with Safavid Iran (f150b-end). Illuminated first two pages. Ruled margins. Foliation in red.
bibliography: bibl: As for Codrington/Reade No 114 (2).; Perhaps still the earliest known MS of the Garbled Memoirs.; For the provenance see Donations Register for November 18 1848.

bibliography: note(s): F1a, slip: Presented by Sir George Staunton Bart.Feb 7. 1824. The name printed, the remainder handwritten. Bound in towards the end: a) A note recording the birth of a son on Sunday 4 Dhu 'l-Qa'dah 1172, and omens taken from the Qur'an in connection with the birth. b) Two narrow slips with square grids filled with numbers, probably magic squares, etc. c) A third similar slip is inserted loose. Bound in after the colophon: a) A copy of the Pandnamah supposedly of Sa'di (10 ff.), the first recto covered with assorted prayers, verses, etc. b) A folio containing copies of two letters, trimmed off at the edges, concerned with the shipment of goods. The ports of Hugli and Chinapatan mentioned. Margins, dividing panels and the final verses of poems in red. Illuminated panel above opening of text.
bibliography: bibl: As for Codrington/Reade Nos 264 and 265.; This is Morley Handwritten Catalogue No 198. Some later hand has erroneously added to the entry there.

work: title: Akhbarat.
paratext: incipit: Incipit, I, after heading: Hadrat-i jahan-panah Muhammad Akbar Shah Padishah-i Ghazi Incipit, II, after date: Khabar-i Maharaha Sahib Maharaja Ranjit Singh Bahadur

I) According to the list of contents, contains reports from Delhi from 12 December 1831 to 18 May 1835, and from Ludhiana 17 January 1835 to 5 December 1835.
bibliography: bibl: None. Likely to be unique, though other collections of Akhbarat survive.

work: title: Zubdat al-tawārīkh; زبدة التواريخ; Majma‘ al-tawārīkh; مجمع التواريخ; Tārīkh-i Ḥaydarī; تاريخ حيدري

paratext: incipit: Dhikr-i ankih awwal mawjud gasht
bibliography: note(s): The manuscript lacks a preface. Above the text on f1b a note in blue pencil identifies it as the Mir'at al-Adwar of of Muslih al-din Lari, incorrectly. Over this is another in black ink identifying it as the Zubdat al-Tawarikh of Haidar(-i) 'Ali Husaini Razi which appears to be correct. F1a. Signature of Ellis, and date 25.3.02 Inserted loose near the beginning is a table of contents in the hand of Ellis. The first volume of a large general history, beginning with the creation and ending with Mamliks of Egypt. Headings in red.
bibliography: bibl: Storey, i, p. 124.; Rieu, Suppt. pp. 20-22. Cf. I, pp. 887-8.

work: title: Kullīyāt-i Khāqānī; كليات خاقانی
author: name(s): Khāqānī, Afz̤al al-Dīn Shirvānī, ca. 1126-1198 or 9 خاقانى ، افضل الدين شروانى
paratext: incipit: Incipit, illuminated page: Khair ma i'tasama al-mar' bih[ib]alihi
bibliography: note(s): (The prose preface to the Tuhfat al-'Iraqain, the verse of which appears to be lacking.) F1a: a) Signature of David Price 1794. b) Note of acquisition from Hajji Kazim. c) Obscure note dated 2 Dhu 'l-Qa'dah regnal year 3. Comprises the qasidahs, tbe muqatta'at, and the diwan. A manuscript of high quality. Ruled margins and dividing panels in gold and colours, the panels filled with floral scrolls on a gold background. Headings in white outlined with black. Twelve pages of particularly rich illumination, at the beginning and the openings of sections of the work. The first two, preceding the illumination title opening have lively scenes of princely hunting and hawking, presumably Safavid and from the earlier part of the sixteenth century. Nearly all the figures wear the taj with the tall baton. These miniatures are not in Robinson's catalogue.

work: title: al-Kāmil al-bahā’ī fī al-Saqīfah; الكامل البهائي في السقيفة
author: name(s): ʻImād al-Dīn Ṭabarī, al-Ḥasan ibn ʻAlī عماد الدين طبري، الحسن بن علي
paratext: incipit: Subhan-i yaki padishahi kih bisat-i 'azamat-i u
bibliography: note(s): F1b: Impression of small oval seal of Hidayatallah, dated A.H. 1280. F1a and the preceding folio, the verso of the last folio of text and the subsequent folio bear notes in various scripts, most of which appear to have been carefully copied from the original. Only a few are noted here. F1a: a) Chronogram of the death of Karim Khan Zand, 1193. b) Four ruba'is, two said to in the hand of Mir 'Imad. Last folio of text, verso: a poem attributed to 'Ali with date 1284. It is possible that the date in the colophon and the name of the scribe come from the MS copied rather than this one. Final blank folio, verso: a ruba'i by Sam Mirza. A work of Shi'i polemic, refuting many of the tenets of the Sunnis. The title presumably alludes to the son of the famous minister Shams al-Din Juwaini son, Baha' al-Din Muhammad, governor of Isfahan, who is eulogised in the introduction as the author's patron and at whose invitation the author taught there for some time in A.H. 672. Ruled margins. Headings in red. The scribe is Baqir al-Husaini al-Taliqani Ardakani. (Unless he was the scribe of the MS copied.)
bibliography: bibl: None found. The work appears to be uncommon.

work: title: Kifayat al-Atibba.
author: name(s): Abu Ji? (Abu Hayy?) b. Husam al-din TY*Y? (BTYNY?).
paratext: incipit: Amma ba'd in kitabist musamma bi-kifayat al-atibba
bibliography: note(s): F1a. Partly effaced impression of a large round Persian seal, probably seventeenth or eighteenth century beside a largely effaced note concerning the book. Leaf attached before f1, recto: a) medical prescriptions. b) Note of possession in red naskh above two faint impressions in red of the seal of Muhammad Taqi, dated A.H. 1266, as on 511(525)b. Folios now loose; kept tied between two pieces of English cardboard. Some notes by Ellis on used envelopes and a paper with a prayer and a charm in Arabic and Persian are included. A comprehensive medical work in twenty books, stated in the preface to include translations from Indian works. The main text is preceded by a table of contents. Headings and ruled margins in red.
bibliography: bibl: Storey, ii, p. 321. Evidently the work is uncommon.

work: title: Khusraw va Shīrīn; خسرو وشيرين

paratext: incipit: Khudawanda bi-'ishqam zindagi dih
bibliography: note(s): F1a, stamp, the name entered in ink: Presented to the ROYAL ASIATIC SOCIETY by Lt Col. C.J. Doyle. A manuscript of sumptuous quality. A panel of illumination above the opening of the text, smaller ones on last two folios, headings in white on gold. Elaborate borders many based on stencils. Six miniatures and one tinted drawing. For the miniatures, marginal decoration and illumination see B.W. Robinson, Persian Paintings in the Collection of the Royal Asiatic Society, pp. 59-61. Entered in the Donations Register for 15 March 1834. No 6 in list of Persian MSS. Here, and for long afterwords, wrongly identified as the Khusrau wa Shirin of Nizami. The correct attribution is supplied in pencil by B.W. R[obinson] on the Library copy of Codrington.
bibliography: bibl: Encyclopaedia of Islam, s.v. Hatifi.; Rieu, Suppt., p. 190.; C.f., Rieu, ii, pp. 652-3; Ethe, No 1398.

work: title: ʻĀlamgīrnāmah; عالمگیرنامه
author: name(s): Muḥammad Kāz̤im ibn Muḥammad Amīn
paratext: incipit: Ay dadah bi-'aql partau-i agahi
bibliography: note(s): Folio one, recto: a) Note of ownership of Abu 'l-Fadl, entitled Fadlallah Khan b. Ghiyath al-Din Mansur al-Hasani al-Husaini al-Anjawi. Impression of his large and finely engraved round seal dated 1108, and 40th regnal year (of Aurangzib, who is mentioned in the inscription. b) Impression of small rectangular seal of Charlz War Malit, dated 1196. In his handwritten catalogue Morley gave the date as 'AH 1102, or perhaps 1152', but then crossed out '1102, or perhaps'. However, the evidence of Fadlallah Khan's seal shows that the earlier date is correct. This MS is then earlier than any of those listed by Storey. Illuminated panel above beginning of text. Headings and punctuation in red.

A history of the first ten years of Shah Jahan's reign. Scribe may be 'Awad 'Ali Khan. Illuminated initial opening. Ruled margins. Red headings and punctuation.

work: title: Marzubānʹnāmah; مرزبان نامه
author: name(s): Marzubān ibn Rustam, active 11th century مرزبان بن رستم
paratext: incipit: Hamd u thana'i kih rawa'ih-i dhikr-i an
bibliography: note(s): Folio after text, recto, stamp, the name and date written in ink: Presented to the ROYAL ASIATIC SOCIETY by J Romer Esq 1 April 1837. Two folios preceding the text contain a note on the work in English, and a similar one in Persian, with some passages copied from the work itself. The Persian part was written at the command of Mr John Romer, Sardar of the port of Surat, and chief judge of the Sadr-i 'Adalat by Ali Akbar, known as Mirza Jan b. the late Mirza Mahdi Isfahani, son of the late Faris? Khan, who was Sarrishtahdar of the Sadr-i 'Adalat so long as the Persian office was active and afterwards a pensioner of the Company Bahadur. This is dated Monday 24 January 1825, 4 Jumada al-Thani 1240. A book of moralising fables, in many ofwhich animals play a part. Translated into ornamental prose by Sa'd al-Din Warawini from the.tenth-century original, written in the dialect of Tabaristan. Red headings and punctuation.
bibliography: bibl: Rieu, Suppt. pp. 239-40.; For the provenance see Donations Register for April 1 1837

work: title: Ḥusaynī-Shāhī

bibliography: note(s): The title given above occurs on the rectos of the second and third front flyleaves, but not in the work itself. He points out that on p. 48 the date given in the colophon is referred to as the present, indicating, as is indeed stated in the colophon, that the work was hastily compiled. Seemingly this is the author's original. Query? Was Ellis in Bombay at this date. Bound with Codrington/Reade No 74 (2). A history of the Afghans from their conquest of Persia to 1224/1809, with descriptions of towns and tribes at the end. Written at the request of Mr Ellis, who had been (? was?) The text is preceded by an opening with two fine illuminated roundels. The left hand one seemingly had an inscription which has been effaced. The first opening of the preface is richly illuminated, the first opening of verse also illuminated.

The previous brown leather covers, Indian and decorated with silver-stamped decoration, are kept with the manuscript. The central stamp on the covers is inscribed with the rebus 'Amal-i Gul Muhammad. Ruled margins and dividing panels. Headings in red. Illuminated initial opening to each of the six books, the left hand folio of that of the first book missing and the text replaced in different hand.

work: title: Dīvān-i Jāmī
paratext: incipit: Incipit of the first section: Bismillah al-rahman al-rahim a'zam asma' 'alim hakim. Incipit of the introduction to the second section: Bismillah al-rahman al-rahim * umli hamd al-mannani 'l-karim. Complete.
bibliography: note(s): F1a: a) In the hand of David Price: this book was purchased at Serungaputtum in July 1799. b) Note of acquisition by 'the slave of the court' at Akbarabad on 1 Rabi' II 1047, headed 'Allahu Akbar'. c) Defaced notes and several seal-impressions. Final folio, verso, on later backing: verse appropriate to the completion of a manuscript written by Muhammad Khanjahan. This MS contains two sections, the second of which has a mainly prose preface in which Jami records that in 884 his scattered verse was written down. In fact 884 in this and other MSS has been shown to be an error for 894. In either case the date is later than that in the colophon which must be incorrect, although it has not obviously been tampered with. References to the poet in the headings to many poems refer to him as alive. The first section contains the second part of the so-called first divan, containing the shorter poems, but lacks the prose preface. The section has the so-called second divan. A manuscript of good quality. Ruled margins and dividing panels. Headings etc in gold and blue. Panels of illumination above the opening page of each section.
bibliography: bibl: Cf. Rieu, ii, p. 644 (Add. 7774).; Ethe, No 1307

work: title: Tarikh i Firishtah, or Gulshan i Ibrahimi.
author: name(s): Firishtah, Muḥammad Qāsim Hindū Shāh Astarābādī فرشته، محمد قاسم هندوشاه استرابادي
paratext: incipit: Incipit (Page 13): Pish i wujud i hama ayandagan * bish i baqayi hama payandagan Sitayish i mutawafira wa niyayish i mutakathira
bibliography: note(s): In several hands. Some quite extensive marginal notes. On European paper with a variety of watermarks, one dated 1815, one 1816. Folio one, recto (numbered page 2): The newly collated edition of the works of Mahomed Kasim Ferishta completed by Lieut. Colonel Briggs. 1826. Deposited for security in the library of the Royal Asiatic Society 13. March 1828. Pages 3-12 contain a preface in ornate style by Khairat 'Ali Khan 'Mushtaq'. This gives a biographical sketchof Firishta. The writer collaborated on the edition of the work with Briggs, who is mentioned on pages 11 and 12. The date A.H. 1241 (1825-6)is given at the end. Pages 1204-1232 contain a vocabulary, given the title Farhang i Brigzi with an introduction by Mushtaq. Neither of these is in the 1831-2 Bombay and Poona edition of Briggs and Mushtaq. The relationship of this MS and the printed edition is not clear. It was given to the Society some years before the edition was printed. Briggs did not retire from service in `India until 1835. A general history of India. There are two different recensions. This MS belongs to the earlier one, in which the whole is subdivided into two books. (See Rieu) Rubricated headings and punctuation. Many of the headings left empty.
bibliography: bibl: Storey, i, 442-50.; Rieu, i, pp. 225-6.; Ethe, No 291.

work: title: Lidhdhat al-'Aish-i Nasir Shahi.
author: name(s): Hakim Muhammad.
paratext: incipit: ... al-istikhara min Allah al-'alim al-hakim
bibliography: note(s): Lacks a folio or two at the beginning. Breaks off at the beginning of the tenth section. Folio preceding text, verso: a note in Persian describing the work, but not naming the author. Bound and uniform with Ellis Uncatalogued 3 (a) and in the same hand. A treatise on sexual intercourse in ten sections. Author is probably Hakim Muhammad (see Notes and References). Headings and punctuation in red.
bibliography: bibl: Storey, ii, p. 234, presumably refers to this work though the title is not given. Only one manuscript is recorded by Storey.

work: title: Mas̲navī; مثنوی
author: name(s): Jalāl al-Dīn Rūmī جلال الدین رومی
paratext: incipit: Hadha kitab al-mathnawi wa hu usul usul usul al-din
bibliography: note(s): The text is preceded by a detailed list of contents uniform with the main text (7ff). Folio with beginning of verse, recto: impression of seal of Iqtidar Husain, date undeciphered. Second blank folio preceding text, verso: note recording ownership of Iqtidar Khan, signed 'Inayat. Sixth blank folio, recto: This book was purchased at Serungaputtun in July 1799 by David Price. Verso: instructions on taking omens from the Mathnawi. Seventh blank folio, recto: verses by Mir Ja'far Nishapuri. FIa, recto: Note recording that the MS was purchased a Murshidabad, known as Makhsusabad, in Bengal for 161? rupees and that it was collated and most of the marginal notes written in Ramadan 1136 (May-June 1724). A fairly lavishly decorated manuscript. Gold and coloured ruled margins and dividing panels. Headings in red. The first ten pages are illuminated, with text framed with gold The name of the scribe and year are given in the colophons of the first five books. The day only in the final colophon.

work: title: Tadhkirat al-Salāṭīn-i Chaghatā; تذكرة السلاطين چغتای
author: name(s): Kāmwar Khān, Muḥammad Hādī Muḥammad Hādī Kāmwar Khān كامور خان، محمد هادي
paratext: incipit: Bar arbab-i khibrat makhfi u muhtahab namanad
bibliography: note(s): The text ends rather abruptly in the middle of a page. Part of the same work as Codrington/Reade No 100. Vol. II. From Jahangir to tbe seventh year of Muhammad Shah, A.H. 1137 (A.D. 1724). Ruled margins. Headings and punctuation in red.

work: title: Akbar-namah.
author: name(s): Abū al-Faz̤l ibn Mubārak, 1551-1602 ابو الفضل بن مبارك علامی
paratext: incipit: Allahu Akbar in chih daryaftist zharf u shinakhti shigarf
bibliography: note(s): The first six folios of text are on different paper and in a hand that is probably later. The rest are on similar paper, but the scribe of Daftar 1 is less accomplished than that of Daftar II. Folio one, recto: Signature of David Price. Bound in between second and third flyleaves is a sheet of paper with, on the recto, what appears to be a passage of draft translation, probably in Price's hand, and, on the verso financial calculations in sterling. Marginal notes and glosses in Persian, and notes in pen and pencil in English, presumably written by Price. Below final colophon, impression of small round seal: Bandah-i Al-i Muhammad Taqi. Final folio, verso, three seal impressions: a) Same as above. b) Small, elongated: Bandah-i Al-i Muhammad Hashim. c) Small, round. Not read. Third and fourth folios, rectos, assorted notes, presumably written by Price. Vol. I. Parts 1 and 2. Containing the history to A.H. 979. Part of the same work as Codrington/Reade No 114 (1). Some rubricated headings. Crude astrological diagrams in the section on Akbar's horoscope.

work: title: Shāhjahān′nāmah; شاهجهان نامه; Mulakhkhaṣ; ملخص
author: name(s): ʻInāyat Khān, ca. 1627-1670 or 71 .
paratext: incipit: بنام پادشاه پاشاهان
bibliography: note(s): The pages repaired with strips of paper along the inner edge. Defective at end, the text breaking off in the twentieth year of the reign. Fromt flyleaf, recto: Presented to the Oriental Translation Committee by Sir A Malet Baronet Inside back cover: armorial bookplate of Sir Chas Warre Malet. Between blank leaves at end there are two slips of blue paper with list of contents of two copies of another Indian historical work, with numbers that do not correspond to anything in the Society's catalogue. A history of the first thirty years of the reign of Shah Jahan, abbreviated from the earlier chronicles of the reign. Headings and punctuation in red.
bibliography: bibl: Storey, i, pp. 577-8.; Rieu, i, pp. 261-2.; Ethe, No 331.

work: title: Mihr va-Mushtarī; مهر و مشتری
author: name(s): ʻAṣṣār Tabrīzī, Muḥammad, d. 1382 or 3 عصار تبريزى، محمد
paratext: incipit: Bi-nam-i padishah-i 'alam-i 'ishq
bibliography: note(s): F1a: impressions of seals of Ibrahim Qutbshah, Muhammad Quli Qutbshah, Muhammad Qutbshah, dated 1021? (1612-13?), Sultan Muhammad dated 1117? (1705-6?), Hajji Rajab 'Ali, dated 1187 (1773-4), Ibrahim, dated 1213 (1798-9). Folio preceding text, recto, in pencil: Đ3.3.0 Verso: a) Purchased by the Oriental Translation Committee b) Two impressions of the seal of Sultan Muhammad noted above. Written diagonally in the margins of ff6-23 is a section of a mathnawi telling of the love of Mahmud and Ayaz, so far unidentified. Ruled margins and dividing panels. Headings in red. Illuminated panel over beginning of text. Rather crude later dividing panels on ff6-16, some with painted flowers.

work: title: Mafātīḥ al-I‘jāz; مفاتیح العجاز
author: name(s): Lāhījī, Muḥammad ibn Yaḥyá, active 15th century لاهيجى، محمد بن يحيى

bibliography: note(s): A commentary on the Gulshan-i Rāz of گلشن راز Shabistarī, Maḥmūd ibn ʻAbd al-Karīm, -approximately 1320 Copied at the command of Mirza Rida Khan Beg Safawi.شبستری ; According to the colophon, copied from a MS written eleven years after the original was composed (in A.H. 877). Front flyleaf, verso: armorial bookplate of Gordon of Buthlaw. A commentary on the Gulshan-i Raz of Mahmud Shabistari. Ruled margins. Headings and punctuation in red. Paper of text area sprinkled with gold. Illuminated panel above opening of text. Scribe's poetic name is 'Jununi'.
bibliography: bibl: Ethe No 1816.; General Gordon's bequest of books and Turkish, Perian and Arabic manuscripts is mentioned, without details in the Donations Register under November 6 1841. The bequest is mentioned in J.R.A.S., vii, 1843, Annual Report, p. x, and the manuscripts are briefly listed in the Proceedings, pp. xxx-xxxi.

work: title: Diwan of Jalal-i Tabib.
author: name(s): Jalal al-Din Ahmad Tabib, known as Jalal-i Tabib.
paratext: incipit: Incipit, of Bab II: Chu shah-i haft kishwar shud zi chakh-i charumin paida.
bibliography: note(s): Folios are missing or bound out of order. Main headings are 1) Bab II, mulamma'at ('macaronic' poems); Qism III, Persian poems. 3) Bab 1, Arabic poems. 4) Kitab-i Gul u Nauruz (a mathnawi. The original final of 4) has been pasted to the verso of the heading upside down. It had a date, which is now illegible. The end of 4) is supplied on two folios in a more recent hand with a colophon date Sha'ban 1235. F1a: vii James Mitchell (Mr Mitchell in pencil on the facing page). An early manuscript of good quality, though now defective. Margins and dividers in gold and black. Headings in gold and black for the most part. Others evidently added later, in red or black. Main headings on illuminated panels.

work: title: Humay wa Humayun.

paratext: incipit: Bi-nam-i khudawand-i bala wa past

author: name(s): Anon.
paratext: incipit: Ahl-i dilan-ra nam-i Khudawand, jallat asma'uhu, kilid-i ganj-i dil ast
bibliography: note(s): Occupies ff90-107 of the manuscript. For further details see Codrington/Reade No 210 (1). In the colophon it is stated that the original name of the work was Parjatak (diacriticals uncertain), and in the the title given on the page preceding the text the same word occurs in an obscure phrase interpreted by Staunton to mean the book (meaning the whole manuscript) was translated. However, the first chapter of this last text deals with Persian music and the work is clearly not translated from Sanskrit or Arabic. A treatise on Persian and Indian music, in an introduction and four chapters. Contains a number of diagrams of stringed instruments in red.

work: title: A short history of the Sikhs from the time of Nanak to A.D. 1806.

paratext: incipit: Ba'd hamd-i Khuda miguyad faqir Bakhtmal
bibliography: note(s): On the fold-out sheet attached to the verso of the first front flyleaf is a description of the work by E.G. Browne. Presumably this is it. It is not unlikely that it came to the Library with Malcolm's other manuscripts, but there is no confirmation. Bound with Codrington/Reade No 74 (1). Written at the desire of Mr (later Sir) John Malcolm. Some gaps left for headings.

work: title: Kulliyāt; كليات
author: name(s): Saʻdī سعدى
paratext: incipit: Shukr u sipas ma'budi-ra jallat qadruhu
bibliography: note(s): F1a: a) Impression of rectangular seal of Archibald Swinton Rustam Jang Bahadur, dated 1174 (1760-1). b) impression of small seal of Sulaiman, dated 1146? (1733-4) and regnal year 4. c) No (1) Kooliat Shaik Saddee a Present from Meer Sulyman d) Stamp, the name filled in in ink: Presented to the ROYAL ASIATIC SOCIETY by Thos. Newnham Esq 15 June 1839. e) Inspection notes dated 19 Rajab 1150 (12 November 1737; regnal year 2 of Muhammad Shah; regnal years 30 and 31. Ruled margins. Headings and punctuation in red. Illuminated openings at beginning of text and ff. 99-100, 171-2, 205-6, 279-80, 306-7 and occasional other illuminated panels. Two openings of miniature paintings have been added at the beginning and end of the text. They are not part of the original MS. The first picture shows a scene of dervishes dancing, the second an incident in a bath-house. The second pair form a single composition depicting a prince at pleasure. These are not covered in Robinson's book on the Society's Persian paintings. They may be seventeenth-century Bukharan work.

work: title: Haft Aurang.
author: name(s): Jāmī, 1414-1492 جامى، عبد الرحمن

In the colophon the scribe states that he copied the book when he was between seventy and eighty and was enabled to alleviate his neediness and provide for his family by this work. The collection of the seven long poems of Jami. Ruled margins and dividing panels. Illuminated panel above the beginning of each poem. Red headings and punctuation.
bibliography: bibl: Rieu, ii, pp. 643-5.; Ethe, No 1300.; Encyclopaedia of Islam, s.v. Djami.

work: title: Tamhidat.
author: name(s): Abu 'l-Ma'ali 'Abdallah b. Muhammad al-Miyanaji (known as 'Ayn al-Qudat Hamadani).

work: title: ʻĀlamgīrnāmah; عالمگیرنامه

work: title: Kulliyāt; كليات

work: title: Dīvān-i Ḥāfiẓ; دیوان حافظ

work: title: Makhzan al-Asrar.
author: name(s): Niẓāmī Ganjavī, 1140 or 41-1202 or 3 نظامى گنجوى
paratext: incipit: Bismi 'llahi 'l-rahmani 'l-rahim

On f1a there is an illuminated roundel, much rubbed, with an illegible central inscription. This has been cut out of another page and pasted on to the backing which supports the original text on f1b. work: title: Habib al-siyar. First two chapters of Vol. Ill.
author: name(s): Khvānd Mīr, Ghiyās̲ al-Dīn ibn Humām al-Dīn, ca. 1475-1535? خواند مير، غياث الدين بن همام الدين
paratext: incipit: Ya rabb bi-thana-yi khwud sukhansazam kun
bibliography: note(s): Second flyleaf has title etc and notes in English. One states that the MS appears to have belonged to Nawwab Sayyid Husain 'Ali Khan Amir al-Umara, one of the famous brothers, i.e. the Sayyids of Barha. A second note written smaller and with different ink, but seemingly by the same hand, which is probably that of David Price, correctly identifies Khwand-amir as Mir Khwand's nephew rather than son. This ends: note on the inside cover of the owners MC?SS - nury? - David Price Folio 1, recto: note in Persian: Sarkar-i Nawwab Husain 'Ali Khan Amir al-Umara. Second note: Si u du juz chahar waraq (32 gatherings 4 pages). Part of the same work as Codrington/Reade No 46. As for Codrington/Reade No 46. For Price's bequest see J.R.A.S. 1834 pp., vi, lxxvi-ii. (Reference from Robinson. Last two pages not in the Library copy) and 1836, pp. xii-xiv (an obituary note p. lx). Headings in red. Ruled margins. Fine illuminated panel above beginning of text.

work: title: Tārīkh-i Manṣūrī; تاريخ منصوري
author: name(s): Ḥusaynī Vāsiṭī Bilgrāmī, ʻAlī ibn Ṭufayl ʻAlī Khān, active 19th century ʻAlī ibn Ṭufayl ʻAlī ibn Mubāriz al-Mulk حسيني واسطى بلگرامى، علي بن طفيل علي خان
paratext: incipit: Sipas-i afzun az hadd [wa] ahadi-ra rawast
bibliography: note(s): Third front flyleaf, verso bears a pasted-on sheet with a description of the work and the gift of it to the Society in Persian, with an impression of the seal of Nawwab Nazir Sidi Darab 'Ali Khan, dated 1238. Before the body of the text, from which it is separated by 3 blank folios is a llst of contents, similar in format to the main text, but less carefully written. Folio one of the list of contents, recto, bears a similar sheet with a similar inscription in English, with the impression of the same seal, which also appears on ff1b, 279a. The author is not Nawwab Nazir Sidi Darab 'Ali Khan, as Codrington says. A history of Bengal, and in particular of the Nawwabs of Murshidabad. For author's name see F2b. The scribe is also the author (see F.279a) Written at the prompting of Darab 'Ali Khan, when the new Company agent, George Hall Macgregor, was asking for information about the history of Bengal. (f3a). Mansur 'Ali Khan is mentioned as the Nawwab at the time of composition (f3b), but the work does not seem in fact to be dedicated to him as Storey states. Ruled margins. Rubricated headings and punctuation.
bibliography: bibl: Storey, i, pp. 721-2.; The only other MSS in Storey are in the library of the Asiatic Society of Bengal and said to derive from this one. Description, extracts with translations: H. Blochmann, Journal of the Asiatic Society of Bengal, xxxvi (1867-8), pp. 85-104. Entered in Donations Register for November 30 1868.

work: title: Basatin al-Salatin.
author: name(s): Ghulam Murtada, called Sahib Hadrat.
paratext: incipit: Sipas-i gunagun wa sitayish-i az hadd afzun mar sani'i-ra
bibliography: note(s): Pale blue watermarked paper. In the preface it is stated the Muhammad Ibrahim al-Zubairi, is the writer - muharrir, tending to be used of scribes rather than authors - of this work. However, at the end of the text the transmitter (naql kunandah), presumably the scribe, who gives his name as Mir Haidar grandson of Mir Ghulam Husain, great grandson? of Nizam al-Mulk Dakhani and Hakim Shams al-Din, notes that the book was composed (ta'lif) by Sahib Hadrat, son-in-law of Shah 'Abdullah Husaini and copied at the command of Briggs Sahib. Ghulam Murtada is named as the author in the copies in the British Museum, and this is confirmed by William Erskine, who knew the author, as noted on a MS dated 1237/1822 which he possessed. In the concluding section 1833 is said to be eight years before the present. In the British Library MSS the present is placed four years after 1833. See Rieu. Inside front cover, printed slip: Lieut. Col. Briggs. A history of the 'Adil-Shahi dynasty to A.H. 1111, with a brief section on later events.
bibliography: bibl: Storey, i, pp. 745-6.; Rieu, i, pp. 319-20.; Ethe, No 456.

work: title: Tadhkirah-i Masha'ikh-i Siwistan.
author: name(s): 'Abd al-Ghafur b. Haidar.
paratext: incipit: Sipas-i bi-qiyas khudawandi-ra kih
bibliography: note(s): The verso of the final folio contains the beginning of an anecdote concerning Shah Bu 'Ali Qalandarin the hand of the same scribe, but the end of this is missing. Many marginal additions in the earlier part. F1a: Various notes and verses. Folio preceding text, recto: a) Signature of Ellis, dated 18.3.09. b) Note in Persian describing the work. Final folio of Ellis Uncatalogued 3 (b), verso, In Ellis's hand: Luzac (Sotheby-Alexander) Contains, loose, a note by Simon Digby describing the work and its publication. Bound with Ellis Uncatalogued 3 (b) and in the same hand. A biographical dictionary of Sufi shaikhs of Siwistan (Sehwan) compiled from oral and written materials and prompted by the visit to the town of Sayyid Muhammad Bahwah?, known as Dindar Khan Ghazi. Headings and punctuation in red.
bibliography: bibl: Not in Storey.; The text was published with the assistance of a microfilm of this manuscript by Pir Hussamuddin Rashdi in Mihran (Karachi), probably in the 1970s.

work: title: Habib al-siyar. First chapter of the second volume.
author: name(s): Khvānd Mīr, Ghiyās̲ al-Dīn ibn Humām al-Dīn, ca. 1475-1535? خواند مير، غياث الدين بن همام الدين
paratext: incipit: Al-hamdu lillah alladhi ja'ala lilnabiyyin lisan sidq 'aliiyyan
bibliography: note(s): Bound up with Codrington/Reade No. 19, which it follows. A different scribe. See that entry for further details. Part of the same work as Codrington/Reade No. 46. Illuminated panel on f1b. Ruled margins covering join of paper of text and margins. Red and gold rubrication.

work: title: Mihr va-Mushtarī; مهر و مشتری
author: name(s): ʻAṣṣār Tabrīzī, Muḥammad, d. 1382 or 3 عصار تبريزى، محمد
paratext: incipit: Bi-nam-i padishah-i 'alam-i 'ishq
bibliography: note(s): The initial entry is written on the Library copy of Codrington. F1a bears notes and seal impressions showing that the MS was in the Mughal Library, where it was valued at 500 mohurs, from the reign of Akbar. A description of the MS, probably dating from its entry into the Library but partially lost under repairs, states that it had been the property of Bihbud Aqa and was now transferred to Luqman. Seals include those of Abu '-Fath Fathallah, dated 1106 (1694-5) and Karim, dated 1058 (1648-9) and regnal year 22. More could be identified. Check if Seyller dealt with this. Inside front cover: Repaired and re-bound in 1966. Ruled margins. Illuminated headings. Illuminated initial opening, showing a stork at the upper right. Two full-page miniatures in late sixteenth-century Shiraz style. See Robinson, Persian Paintings in the Collection of the Royal Asiatic Society, pp. 57-8.
bibliography: bibl: As for Codrington/Reade No 303.; Also B.W. Robinson, Persian Paintings in the Collection of the Royal Asiatic Society, pp.57-8.

work: title: Khamsah.
author: name(s): Niẓāmī Ganjavī, 1140 or 41-1202 or 3 نظامى گنجوى
paratext: incipit: Khudawanda rah-i taufiq bigshay
bibliography: note(s): The initial entry is a handwritten addition to the Library copy of Codrington. This page, as indicated in the panel of illumination, is the beginning of Khusrau wa Shirin, but is bound out of place. The first poem is in fact the Makhzan al-Asrar, the beginning of which is missing. The manuscript was conserved in 1967 by Roger Powell (So Robinson). A typewritten note of the details of the work, initialled R.P.W. is pastedinside the back cover. Two sheets containing notes on the pages missing from the manuscript are inside the front cover. The five long poems of Nizami. A manuscript of good quality but with many of the original miniatures and much of the illumination removed. Ruled blue, red and black margins. Illuminated panel above beginning of text. Headings in blue on vegetal scrolling, which also occurs by the colophon an elsewhere. Thirteen miniatures in Shiraz style remain. See B.W. Robinson, Persian Paintings in the Collection of the Royal Asiatic Society, pp. 29-30. Robinson also gives a list of the pages that have been removed.

work: title: Sharāʼiʻ al-Islām; al-Sharʻah al-aḥkam; شرائع الاسلام; الشرعة الاحكم
author: name(s): Muḥaqqiq al-Ḥillī, Jaʻfar ibn al-Ḥasan, 1205 or 6-1277 المحقق الحلي، جعفر بن الحسن

work: title: Ḥāshiyat al-Quṭbī; حاشية القطبي
author: name(s): Jurjānī, ʻAlī ibn Muḥammad, al-Sayyid al-Sharīf, 1340-1413 الجرجاني، علي بن محمد، السيد الشريف

work: title: Nān va ḥalvā; نان وحلوا

work: title: Habib al-siyar. Vol.II.
author: name(s): Khvānd Mīr, Ghiyās̲ al-Dīn ibn Humām al-Dīn, ca. 1475-1535? خواند مير، غياث الدين بن همام الدين
paratext: incipit: Rabbana atina min ladunika rahmatan wa hayyi' lana min amrina rushdan. Al-hamdu lillah alladhi ja'ala lilnabiyyin lisan sidq
bibliography: note(s): Front flyleaf, recto: Presented to the Oriental Translation Com[ittee] by Sir A Malet Bart Part of the same work as Codrington/Reade No 46. History of the twelve Imams, the Umayyad and Abbasid Khalifs, and of Dynasties contemporary with the Abbasids. Illuminated panel at top of f1b. Ruled margins and rubrication.

work: title: Akbar-namah.
author: name(s): Abū al-Faz̤l ibn Mubārak, 1551-1602 ابو الفضل بن مبارك علامی
paratext: incipit: Allahu Akbar in chih daryaftist zharf u shinakhtist shigarf
bibliography: note(s): Folio one, recto: Briggs. First flyleaf, recto impression of small rectangular seal: Thakur Parshad (regnal year) 13 (A.H.?) 1248 (?). Also on verso of final flyleaf. Inside front cover, pasted slip: Lieut. Col. Briggs. Vol. I. Parts 1 and 2. Part of the same work as Codrington/Reade No 114 (1). Illuminated panel on first page of text. Ruled margins. Rubricated headings and punctuation. Initial and final sections on pink paper.

work: title: Muntakhab al-Lubāb; Muntakhab-i lubb al-Lubāb; منتخب اللباب
author: name(s): Khāfī Khān, Muḥammad Hāshim, ca. 1663-ca. 1731 خافی خان، محمد هاشم
paratext: incipit: Jahan jahan shukr u sipas afzun az qiyas padshahi-ra sazast
bibliography: note(s): In a note in Persian and one in English on the front flyleaf, recto, the MS is said to be the first volume of Khafi Khan's history and this has been accepted in the Library catalogues, but in the introduction (f1b) the author says he is beginning the second, which is correct. See Storey. Front flyleaf, recto: Presented to the Oriental Translation Come. by Sir A. Malet Bart Inside back cover, armorial bookplate of Sir Cha. Warre Malet. Part one of volume II, containing a brief account of the origin of the house of Timur and the history of the Indian Mughals to A.H. 1067 (A.D. 1656). See notes. Headings and punctuation in red.
bibliography: bibl: Storey, i, pp. 460-470.; Rieu, i, pp. 232-6. Ethe, No 396.; For Sir Alexander Malet's gift see the Transactions for 1830, pp. xxxiv-xxxv.

work: title: Tarikh i Firishtah, or Gulshan-i Ibrahimi.
author: name(s): Firishtah, Muḥammad Qāsim Hindū Shāh Astarābādī فرشته، محمد قاسم هندوشاه استرابادي
paratext: incipit: Pish-i wujud-i hama ayandigan * pish-i baqa-yi hama payandigan (Meaning?)
bibliography: note(s): First free flyleaf, recto which has a fragment pasted on a complete new sheet. On the fragment, Persian notes: a) Note of presentation by Lala Udi Raj (?), dated 27 Jumada II regnal year 5. b) Tarikh i Firishtah tamam (complete). c) Probably associated with this, note of completion for 140 rupees, the amount written in siyaq and words. These are accompanied by English translations (evidently by Briggs). On the rest of the sheet. In Persian: a) Definition of the word mafarr. b) Note concerning China root in the hand of Hakim 'Ali Asghar dated 24 Safar, regnal year 30, A.H. 1160. Folio 1, recto. a) Impression of oblong elliptical seal of Sayyid Qutb al-Din Khan Bahadur. With English translation of the legend by Briggs. b) Impression of large round seal of a fidawi (devotee) of Muhammad Shah dated 1141 (digit uncertain), the bottom half with the name of the owner thoroughly defaced. This is accompanied by a note in English signed J.B. (John Briggs) saying that the writer is unable to decipher the name of the owner of the seal. c) Note recording purchase of the book for the Sarkar (?) on 12 Rajab regnal year 17 of Muhammad Shah, for 185 rupees (written in words and siyaq) including expenses and gratuity. Translation by Briggs, giving the Christian date as 11 October 1736, and translating Sarkar as the King's Library. d) Note with 1146? written in siyaq and said to be the date of Prince Ahmad Shah's move to the Qandahari Afghan, his victory, the death of Muhammad Shah and his vizier Qamar al-Din Khan, killed by a cannon-ball while at prayer? in his tent. Needs checking. f) At top: JM (John Malcolm?) No-52. Last folio, verso. a) A second impression of the seal of Qutb al-Din Khan, with Briggs's translation and hand copy. b) Note of inspection, dated regnal year 21 of Muhammad Shah, with translation. c) Note of inspection in the Library dated Rajab regnal year 21 of Muhammad Shah, with translation. Seal of [a servant of] Muhammad, Shah of Delhi, A.H.1141. Inside front cover, under the folio partly stuck to it: John Johnstone 1765 John Malcolm 1795 to John Briggs 1811. (Written by Malcolm?) Illuminated panel at beginning. Ruled margins. Rubrication.

work: title: Poems of Riyadi.

work: title: Kamil al-Ta'bir.
author: name(s): Abul Fazl Hubaysh (here written Husayn) b. Ibrahim al-Tiflisi.

bibliography: note(s): Incomplete, the text ending abruptly in the entry on 'murdan'. F1a: a) Signature of David Price, dated 1800. b) Note recording presentation of the book by Hakim al-Mamalik Masih al-Dawlah Masih-i Zaman Khan Bahadur to an inferior, the nearby impression of whose seal has been obliterated. work: title: Humay wa Humayun.
author: name(s): Khvājū-yi Kirmānī, Maḥmūd ibn ʻAlī, 1290 or 91-1352? خواجوى كرمانى، محمود بن على، ١٢٩٠-١٣٥٣م
paratext: incipit: Bi-nam-i khudawand-i bala wa past
bibliography: note(s): Last page, recto (f153a): Paris 1830 d'apres un manuscrit de la bibliotheque Royale de Turin par H. Jouy, membre de la Societe Asiatique de Paris. Rue Hauteville no. 12, a Paris. Front flyleaf, verso: Presented to the Oriental Translation Com By His Majesty the King of Sardinia April 16. 1831. Headings in gold..Illuminated panel with title over begining of text. Four full-page miniature paintings, copies of originals in late 16th century Shiraz style. See B.W. Robinson, Persian Paintings in the Collection of the Royal Asiatic Society, pp. 73-5.

work: title: Minhaj al-Yaqin.

bibliography: note(s): F1a: a) Impression of rectangular seal of ... Ibn Murtada 'Ali, dated A.H.1214. b) Partly effaced note with name Mahmud, not the author, presumably an owner. work: title: Minu Khirad.
author: name(s): Marzban (Rawani? so in pencil on the second flyleaf. See notes.).
paratext: incipit: Bi-nam-i khudawand-i jall u jalal
bibliography: note(s): Marzban, apparently the author's name, appears at the end of the first poem and in the heading of the second. Probably also on f9a, where it may be implied that he came from Rawar. First flyleaf, verso: From the Atash Bahman Fire Temple, built at Surat by Peshtanji Kalabhai Wakeel?. Presented by his son Nausheerwanji? to John Romer. March 1856 (The year may be in the Samvat calendar.) Second flyleaf, recto: a) note of ownership of ... Bahramji? Nausheerwanji? ... b) line of Devanagiri-type script. The title is written in pencil in English of the second flyleaf, recto. This is not the Persian translation of the Zoroastrian work of that name (e.g. Ethe No 2986). The MSS consists of two poems, the first consisting mainly of a series of question put by a wise man to Khirad (Wisdom). The second gives an account of some of the activiies of the Sasanian king Anushirwan, of the end of the Sasanian dynasty and negotiations between 'Ali and the Mubads ending in his making a treaty with the Persians. Headings in red.
bibliography: bibl: None found.; Entered in the Donations Register for April 5 1856.

work: title: Mahābhārata; Mahābhārat; مهابهارت
author: name(s): Anonymous
paratext: incipit: Rawiyyan-i akhbar-i Hindustan dar kutub-i khud chunin niwishta and
bibliography: note(s): Translation of vol.I of the Sanskrit epic containing the first six books by Abu 'l-Fadl and others.Commissioned by the Mughal Emperor Akbar. This MS lacks the usual introduction by Abu 'l-Fadl. >Not in Morley Printed Cat. First folio of each book, recto has a note in Persian giving the number of the book and its Sanskrit name, and in some case the number of folios. English notes of contents in pencil in margins. Some Persian scribal corrections and notes. Flyleaf, recto, pencilled title and catalogue Nos. F1a, in ink: David Price. In ink on bottom of pages: Maha Bahrat VOL.1. On spine: title in English; paper labels: [Per]sian (number deleted), 14. In the list of donors in Morley's handwritten catalogue No 72 is listed among the donations of Price and of Lieutenant Alexander Burnes. However this volume is by the same scribe and binder as No 15, and both have Price's signature. N.B. Price translated and published part of the story of Krishna. He also published memoirs. See Buckland. Ruled margins.
bibliography: bibl: Rieu, i, pp. 57-8.; Ethe, No 1928. Gives same incipit.; For Price's bequest see the Journal for 1836, pp. xii-xiv (an obituary note p. lx).

work: title: Jug Bashisht.
paratext: incipit: Sipas u sitayish [wa] tamam niyayish nithar-i hadratist
bibliography: note(s): Not in Morley Printed Cat. Inside front cover: pencil note of Morley catalogue number; ink notes: a) History of the 7th Incarnation of Vishnou, his Expedition to Lanca or Ceylon, for the recovery of his Wife Seeta. b) Translated into Persian from the Sanscrit, of language of the Bramins -- This Book exhibits a fine Specimen of the manner in which the Persian Shekasteh is written -- Flyleaf, recto: in ink: a) From the collection made in India by General Carnac -- (probably in the hand of b) above); b) Presented by the Revd. Dr Macbride Nov 4 1826. Second flyleaf, recto. Title in Persian and English, in Ink, in English in Pencil, adding 'Translation from the Sanskrit. In ink: History of the seventh Incarnation of Vishnou. Labels on spine: a) leather: R.A.S. MS. CAT. 14. b) paper: Persian (14 deleted) 16 History of the Seventh Incarnation of Vishnu??. Translated from the Sanskrit Yogavasishtha traditionaly attributed to Valmiki. A copy of the version commissioned by Darashukuh in A.H. 1066. Ethe and Rieu state that the work is an exposition of Hindu gnosticism in the form of a dialogue. Notes on the inside front cover and second flyleaf recto state this to be an account of the seventh incarnation of Vishnu. This is also given in Morley's Handwritten Catalogue, but Ethe and Rieu say nothing of this. It is stated in the colophon that the first sections were written by Moti Niwal and the last by ...? Gobind Ray.

A Persian dictionary, written at the suggestion of Prince Bahman Mirza for presentation to his brother, the future Muhammad Shah. Ruled and gilded margins. Headings and punctuation in red.

work: title: Mukhtaṣar Buqrāṭ al-ḥakīm fī al-ṭibb; مختصر بقراط لحكيم فى الطب

bibliography: note(s): Contains Persian and Arabic versions of a medical work on medicine in 67 chapters going under the name of Hippocrates. 1) Persian, ff3-36. 2) Arabic, 39-80. And other works. See notes. Semi-literate notes on ff1a, 80b,117b, 140a refer to the copying of the various sections, and perhaps its composition, among a group of residents of BWNKR including ono or more Lahori physicians in A.H. 1240. Headings, punctuation etc. in red.

work: title: Nigaristan.
author: name(s): Ghaffārī, Ahmad ibn Muhammad, ca. 1495-1567 or 8 غفارى، احمد بن محمد
paratext: incipit: Ay tarazanda-yi baharistan way nigaranda-yi nigaristan
bibliography: note(s): Folios one and two have been patced and parts of the text rewritten on the new patches. Folio one, recto. Note of ownership of Mir 'Ali Muhammad al-Sini al-Taliqani b. Mir Muhammad Baqir b. Mir Abu Talib. Stamp with space left for name: Presented to the ROYAL ASIATIC SOCIETY by John Romer Esq. Folio one, verso. Impression of rectangular seal of 'Ali Muhammad al-Husaini, date, if any, illegible. Final folio, verso. Faint impression of rectangular seal inscribed: Bismillah al-Rahman al-Rahim. Date illegible. The date middle of Jumada II A.H. 959 for the completion of the work given at the end of the text is that of the original compostion, not of this copy. This is pointed out in the accompanying pencil note in English. This last gives the date wrongly as 1059, and mistakenly seems to state that Morley said it was the date of copying. It correctly points out that the paper is watermarked, but may be wrong to say it is English foolscap. The watermark seems to contain the initials EM under a device. Occasional pages are on Oriental paper without chainlines. A collection of narratives and notices of Rulers and Celebrated Persons, from the time of Muhammad to the tenth century of tbe Hijrah. Headings in red.
bibliography: bibl: Storey, i, pp. 114-5.; Rieu, i, p. 106.; Ethe, No 606.; Romer's gift is described in the Donations Register for November 18 1848 and the Journal for 1837, p. xiv.

B'bay Army (A similar note on final filio, verso) b) Stamp, the name in ink: Presented to the ROYAL ASIATIC SOCIETY by Major Genl. Bagnold A verse account of the life of Muhammad and the first Caliphs, with the continuation of Muhammad Sadiq Azad. Margins and dividers ruled and gilt. Headings in red with gold infilling. Panels of illumination above beginning of text, beginning of continuation and at one intermediate point. Fourteen fairly simple miniatures in Kashmir style.
